description: EUROAVIA Rzeszów is an aerospace scientific club at the Rzeszów University of Technology (PRz) where students design, build, and test advanced projects like UAVs and rocket components. We bridge academic theory with industry practice through hands-on engineering, international competitions, and technical workshops, preparing members for professional careers.
summary:
Our team developed a comprehensive Streamlit dashboard to tackle the 'Flame in Freefall' challenge by analyzing NASA’s Physical Science Informatics database. We built an interactive data explorer that processes raw experimental data on normal and inverse diffusion flames, generating dynamic thermodynamic charts to evaluate spacecraft atmospheric safety.
To demonstrate the physics of spacecraft fire safety, we integrated 2D Ansys CFD simulations comparing flame behavior across Earth, Mars, Moon, and microgravity environments, visualizing how the lack of buoyancy alters flame shape and species transport. Furthermore, we implemented a Super Intelligence using a RAG architecture. This AI assistant instantly queries the PSI dataset and knowledge base to provide astronauts with real-time, data-driven fire suppression strategies.
This tool is critical because it empowers NASA engineers to design safer Environmental Control and Life Support Systems, manage toxic soot emissions, and establish robust emergency protocols for deep space missions.
Future Vision (Real-Time SimAI): Our ultimate goal is to evolve this platform into a live digital twin by integrating AI-driven CFD surrogate models (such as Ansys SimAI). This would allow the dashboard to instantly predict and visualize microgravity flame propagation and soot distribution on the fly, directly in the browser.
details:
1. How it works & What it does

Our project is an interactive Streamlit-based web dashboard designed to analyze combustion in microgravity. It processes raw NASA Physical Science Informatics datasets and generates thermodynamic charts. Additionally, it features an integrated Super Intelligence Assistant powered by a RAG architecture, allowing users to query the PSI dataset and a custom combustion knowledge base in real-time. We also incorporated custom 2D CFD simulations to visually compare flame structures across varying gravity levels side-by-side.

2. Tools, Languages, and Software Used

  • Programming & Data: Python, Streamlit (UI framework), Pandas.
  • AI Integration: Google Gemini API.
  • Simulation & Engineering: Ansys SpaceClaim and Ansys Fluent. CFD physics included laminar flow, species transport, the energy equation, Stiff Chemistry Solver, and a transient model. We defined specific boundary conditions, a 1500K temperature ignition patch, and precisely tuned under-relaxation factors and species mass fractions to ensure convergence while manipulating gravity from -9.81 m/s² down to 0 m/s².
  • Deployment: GitHub and Streamlit Community Cloud.

3. Benefits & Intended Impact

The platform bridges the gap between raw experimental tables and actionable safety protocols. By instantly correlating oxygen concentration with adiabatic flame temperature and system pressure, it provides critical insights for designing spacecraft Environmental Control and Life Support Systems. The AI serves as a rapid-response tool that could assist engineers and astronauts in formulating data-driven fire suppression strategies during active onboard emergencies.

4. Creativity & Key Factors Considered

Our creativity lies in combining three distinct domains: data science, computational fluid dynamics, and artificial intelligence into a single, accessible hub. We didn't just plot data; we built a system that "understands" it. Key factors our team had to consider included:

  • Data inconsistencies: We engineered robust Python parsers to handle varying column naming conventions in the raw NASA files and hidden whitespace formatting errors.
  • Physics of Microgravity: We specifically separated Normal Diffusion Flames from Inverse Diffusion Flames in the UI to properly isolate and analyze soot formation without the interference of buoyancy-induced flickering.
  • Future Scalability: While this initial prototype focuses on analyzing critical ethylene and ethane tests, future iterations will implement automated data pipelines to ingest the entire spectrum of NASA PSI combustion databases. This will seamlessly transform our dashboard from a targeted prototype into a universal, multi-mission analytical hub.
